mentions.author: bmitc
mentions.story: Ask HN: Any advice on how to learn good software architecture practices?
mentions.text:
There are a lot of good books here: [link]

I second the comment ( [link]) recommending How to Design Programs (HTDP) and Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs (SICP). The former has an edX course ( [course] and [course]) and the latter has online lectures ( [link])

Head First Architecture ( [link]) is good.

Reading about systems thinking would be useful.

Learning programming languages that have been well designed is helpful. I suggest Programming Erlang: Software for a Concurrent World and Elixir in Action.

mentions.author: so-cal-schemer
mentions.story: 9 Years of "Learning to Code" and I Still Couldn't Build a To-Do App
mentions.text:
The author is trying to eat an elephant and doesn't know where to begin. They are trying to learn too many things at once without a foundation to build on.

Start by developing fundamental skills: learn your environment, your editor, your debugger, the syntax of the language.

It's like learning to cook. You need to develop safe knife skills, and learn the best way to cut and portion vegetables. Learn to oil and use a pan and thermometer to thoroughly cook, but not burn, your food. These are fundamental skills that can be learned through observation, but must be practiced through trial and error.

> Debugging is 90% of coding.

> You learn by breaking, not by watching.
